skill_traces.query:
Joanna: Hey Nate, long time no see! The screenplay I sent in to the film festival has been on my mind all day everyday. I keep bouncing between crazy emotions like relief, excitement and worry! Fingers crossed a producer or director falls in love with it and it ends up on the big screen - that would be awesome!
Nate: Hey Joanna! It is a big deal! I'm sure its been a wild ride. Sending some positive vibes and hoping someone likes it enough to get it on the big screen - that would be awesome!
Joanna: Thanks Nate, your support really means a lot. I put a lot of effort into it and I'm crossing my fingers. What about you? Anything new and exciting happening in your life?
Nate: Thanks, Joanna. Not much has changed for me, but I just discovered that I can make coconut milk icecream and gave it a try. It was actually pretty good, so I'm proud of myself.
Joanna: Looks delish! Glad you tried something new and it went well. What did you think of it?
Nate: Super good! It was rich and creamy - might be my new favorite snack!
Joanna: Great! I love when you try something new and it actually works out. Will you give it another go?
Nate: Yep, it could be fun! I'm looking forward to trying out different flavors and toppings.
Joanna: Yum! Sounds great. Got any favorite flavors for dairy-free desserts?
Nate: I love coconut milk, but I also enjoy chocolate and mixed berry flavors.
Joanna: Wow, those sound great! Who can say no to chocolate and berries? I'm tempted to try dairy-free flavors now!
Nate: Well I also made a dairy-free chocolate cake with berries on it the other day, maybe you would like that!
Joanna: Wow! That sounds yummy! You're so talented. Thanks for sharing your amazing creations! I should really try making one or just pay you a visit and try one for myself!
Nate: I couldn't agree more! It's always fun experimenting in the kitchen.
Joanna: I can tell! Your cooking skills are awesome. Seen any good movies lately?
Nate: Not recently. Any good ones you'd recommend?
Joanna: I just watched "Little Women" and it was amazing! It's a great story about sisterhood, love, and reaching for your dreams. Definitely a must-see!
Nate: Oh, that sounds like a great one! I'll definitely add it to my list. Thanks for the recommendation!
Joanna: Anytime! I'm always down to give movie reccomendations.
Nate: Good to know! I'll be sure to give you a shout whenever I run out of things to watch!
Joanna: Sounds great! Let me know what you think of it when your done!
Nate: You bet! You'll be the first to know.
Joanna: Awesome! Enjoy yourself!
Nate: You too, take care!
Joanna: Later, take care!

selected.name: Extract Explicit Preference Statements
selected.description: When a speaker explicitly states a preference, favorite, or strong like/dislike for a specific item or activity, create a preference memory during extraction.
content: During extraction, scan every message for explicit preference expressions (e.g., 'I love', 'my favorite is', 'really into', 'X is beautiful', 'go crazy for') and create a preference candidate for each distinct item or activity mentioned.
Include preferences attributed to the speaker's pets, children, or family as valid memories; record the specific subject and the liked items/activities.
Do not convert explicit enjoyment into a recommendation or event memory; preserve the original preference wording.
Capture preferences from casual, short, or reflective statements, including those with positive affect (e.g., 'awesome', 'so fun') even without 'I like'.
Stop after capturing all explicit preferences; do not infer additional ones beyond what is stated.
selected.rerank_reason: The conversation contains explicit preference statements such as 'I love coconut milk', 'I also enjoy chocolate and mixed berry flavors', and 'I should really try making one or just pay you a visit and try one for myself' which indicate specific likes and preferences.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture likely deceased from euphemistic absence language
nearby_not_selected.description: During extraction, when a speaker describes someone with euphemistic absence language (e.g., 'will never be able to...', 'I miss him/her here') that strongly implies death, use this guidance.
content: When a statement euphemistically implies a person has died without explicitly saying so, also extract the implied state that the person is likely deceased, in addition to the literal statement.
Record the inference with an appropriate hedge (e.g., 'likely deceased') because the speaker did not state it directly; do not assert cause, date, or circumstances of death.
Stop after capturing the likely-deceased state and the literal content; do not extrapolate further details about the person or the relationship.

nearby_not_selected.name: Correct Subject Attribution in Multiparty Messages
nearby_not_selected.description: Use during extraction when a message relays information about another participant's condition, status, or plans, to attribute the memory to the correct person.
content: Before creating a memory from a message, identify the actual subject: the person whose condition, action, or plan is described, not necessarily the speaker.
When a message relays a third party's assessment about another participant, store the fact as a state for that participant, including the quoted assessment.
If the same message contains information about multiple people, create separate memories for each person.

nearby_not_selected.name: Resolve relative time in memory content
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting a memory from a message that contains a relative time expression (e.g., next month, next week, tomorrow), resolve it to the absolute date using the message/session timestamp and include that absolute date in the content.
content: Applies during extraction: when a source message uses a relative time expression (next week, next month, tomorrow, in N days, etc.), resolve it to an absolute date using the message/session timestamp.
Write the resolved absolute date into the memory content itself (e.g., 'September 2023' instead of 'next month'); do not leave the relative phrase in the stored content.
Set world_start (and world_end if applicable) to the same resolved date so content and metadata are consistent.
Stop after resolving the expression; do not add extra details or searches.

nearby_not_selected.name: Preserve Specific Plan Details in Event Memory Extraction
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting an event or plan memory and messages state what participants will try, do, or consume, include those concrete details in the memory content.
content: During extraction of event/plan memories, if messages explicitly state what participants will try, do, or consume (e.g., a specific dish, drink, or activity), preserve those concrete items in the memory content instead of replacing them with a generic label like 'date' or 'meet up'.
When the same plan is mentioned across multiple messages, merge the explicitly stated specifics into one memory record, but do not add details that were not said.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Explicit Advice and Suggestions
nearby_not_selected.description: When a message contains explicit advice, suggestions, or recommendations from one participant to another, extract them as memory candidates.
content: During extraction, treat explicit advice, suggestions, and recommendations as memory-worthy. Capture the advisor, the recipient, the advised action, and the source message.
Preserve all distinct pieces of advice and their qualifiers; do not collapse or omit details. Tentative phrasing still counts.
Represent as an event or relationship memory; create at most one candidate per distinct piece of advice.
Stop after capturing the stated advice; do not infer outcomes or expand into related topics.
